passage: Deepak had written his proposal on a page, and after dinner in the courtyard he read it out to his parents. "Saturday I'd like to go to Gopika's house until eight. I'll give you the address and share my location on the phone. I'll call when I arrive, and one of you picks me up at eight. Let's try it for one month, then we talk." Amma looked at Papa. "Gopika's mother will be home?" "Yes. I'll ask her to speak to you." Papa tapped the page. "The month starts this Saturday. If any part is skipped, we stop." "Deal," said Deepak. His palms were damp. On Saturday he called from the gate, and at eight sharp Papa was outside Gopika's house on the scooter, waving.

qa.q: Until what time did Deepak want to stay at Gopika's house?
qa.a: Deepak wanted to stay until eight.

qa.q: How did Deepak feel while reading the proposal aloud?
qa.a: Deepak was nervous but hopeful; the damp palms show the nerves, and the written page shows how much he wanted it to work.

qa.q: What could Deepak offer if a parent still hesitated, and why?
qa.a: Deepak could offer a shorter first visit or have Gopika's mother phone as well, because extra safeguards answer the worry without ending the trial.

qa.q: How might Papa see the proposal?
qa.a: Papa likely feels reassured, since it covers the address, the call on arrival and the pick-up, and a one-month trial lets him check it works.

grounding: The teen proposes going to a friend's house until 8 pm, sharing the address and location, phoning on arrival and being picked up by a parent, offering a one-month trial.
